notes.1: Most candidates were able to use the key to correctly identify the leaves.
notes.2a: While most candidates were familiar with ingestion and mechanical digestion, fewer were able to correctly identify where protease is produced or where nutrients are absorbed.
notes.2b: (i) Most candidates were able to define what an enzyme is.
notes.2bii: Nearly all candidates could recall one product of fat digestion, fewer knew the second product.
notes.2iii: Careful reading of the question was required as many candidates gave components of fats rather than the required elements.
notes.2iv: Most candidates were able to identify the foods that are good sources of dietary fat.
notes.2v: A good understanding of diet was shown by the majority of candidates.
notes.2vvi: Most candidates were able to give one use of fat in the body.
notes.3a: A good understanding of hormones and the glands producing them was shown.
notes.3b: While most candidates understood that insulin is used to control glucose, fewer were able to explain its role in reducing blood glucose concentration.
notes.3c: All parts of this question were well-answered by the majority of candidates.
notes.3d: (i) Many candidates described how adrenaline makes a person feel, rather than how it affects the body.
notes.3dii: The majority of candidates selected the correct activities. �PAGE�23
notes.4b: (ii) The majority of candidates were able to provide two correct responses. A common error was to state two reactants.
notes.4biii: Many good responses were seen. Errors include giving uses of oxygen rather than uses of energy.
notes.4c: Most candidates were able to give a suitable difference.
notes.4d: This was well-answered by the majority of candidates.
notes.5: Some candidates found this question challenging.
notes.5a: Some candidates were able to label the diagram correctly, others found this more challenging.
notes.5b: Many candidates were able to describe two structural differences. Some candidates misread the question and gave differences in the functions of the blood vessels.
notes.5c: Generally, a good understanding of the functions of the components of blood was shown.
notes.6a: The majority of candidates were able to answer with a tropism; fewer were able to say which one was involved.
notes.6b: An excellent understanding of the conditions required for germination enabled most candidates to provide detailed and correct responses.
notes.6c: (i) Very few candidates were able to give the immediate function of nitrate and magnesium ions, although most understood the requirement for growth and photosynthesis.
notes.6cii: An excellent understanding of the absorption of ions was shown. A few candidates gave responses that explained where the ions travelled once inside the plant rather than how they entered the plant, which was not required.
notes.7a: An excellent understanding of adaptations was shown, with most candidates limiting answers to visible adaptations, as expected.
notes.7b: Candidates found this question challenging and many were unable to describe the process of natural selection. Although there was some were able to explain that some animals would live and some would die, the link to adaptations was not made. A common error was to give a description of selective breeding rather than natural selection.
notes.7c: Overall the majority of candidates provided good responses. For a minority of candidates, there was some confusion over the word ‘endangered’, with some descriptions of why polar bears are dangerous being given rather than why they are an endangered species.
notes.8a: Careful reading was required here. While all candidates could correctly read from the bar chart, some did not reference gender in their responses to both parts of this question.
notes.8b: Candidates showed a very good understanding of the risks of smoking, but could not always distinguish which component caused which effect.
notes.8c: Many candidates gave more effects of smoking, while the question asked for risk factors for coronary heart disease, other than smoking. �PAGE�24
notes.key_messages:
It is essential that candidates consider each question carefully before starting to write their answers.
Candidates should ensure that they are answering the question asked.
